name: Dull Dark Purple
lede: Dull Dark Purple is a muted, reddish purple first plated by Robert Ridgway in 1912, and nearly identical to the crowd-named Dirty Purple a century on.

sections.title: A 1912 plate, echoed by a 2010 survey
sections.body:
Ridgway's *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* of 1912 plates this swatch at plate XXVI, hue 67 prime, on an aged, scanned original that is itself approximate [1]. The name pairs *dull dark* with [[purple]] [1]. At hex #7B4A6C it measures lightness 38 and chroma 28 in LCH, and the nearest ISCC-NBS block reads as a moderate reddish purple, 7.2 units off [1].

Its closest named neighbors are [[dirty-purple|Dirty Purple]] and [[dusky-plum|Dusky Plum]], each 2.6 units away and almost the same color; [[dirty-purple|Dirty Purple]] comes from the unrelated 2010 xkcd survey, nearly a century after this plate, yet lands almost on top of it [2]. [[raisin-purple|Raisin Purple]] sits 3.1 units off, also almost the same [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this purple in 7 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.03 percent, as photographed, among the rarest named colors here [3]. The earliest match is Jacopo Bassano's *Adoration of the Magi*, dated 1568, 344 years before Ridgway's plate, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3]. All of the small number of matches fall in the 1500s and 1800s-1900s, including Paul Gauguin's *The Invocation* of 1903 [3]. These are screen matches on photographs of varnished paintings, not a record of any pigment [3].

origin.named_after: a modifier of purple: dull dark + purple
